title: Wire colours: mains, DC, data and thermostats
summary: What each wire colour usually means in house wiring, cords, PC power supplies, USB, network cable, thermostats and speakers. Colours are a hint, not a guarantee: always test.

steps.text: Never trust a colour in salvaged or old wiring. Test with a meter or a non-contact voltage tester before you touch it.
steps.warn: In North American switch loops a white wire can be live. Treat every wire as live until you have proved it dead.

steps.text: Mark wires with tape and a pen as you disconnect them, or photograph them first.
When you reuse cable, keep green and green-yellow for earth only, so the next person isn’t misled.

notes:
## Mains wiring

| Conductor | North America | Europe and most of the world (IEC) | Old UK fixed wiring (before 2004) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live (hot) | Black, also red | Brown | Red |
| Neutral | White or grey | Blue | Black |
| Earth (ground) | Green, green-yellow or bare | Green-yellow | Green-yellow (older: green) |

- North American polarised plugs: the wider blade is neutral.
- Flat two-wire cord (North America): the ribbed or marked side is neutral, the smooth side is live.
- 240 V circuits in North America have two live wires (often black and red) and may have no neutral.
- In the UK, appliance cords have been brown and blue since the 1970s, and house wiring from 2004 to 2006 can mix the old and new colours.

## DC and vehicles

- Red is usually +, black −. Some old equipment breaks this rule.
- In cars, ground wires are often black or brown; measure before you rely on it.

## USB cable (USB 2.0)

| Colour | Use |
|---|---|
| Red | +5 V |
| Black | Ground |
| Green | Data + |
| White | Data − |

## PC power supply (ATX)

| Colour | Use |
|---|---|
| Yellow | +12 V |
| Red | +5 V |
| Orange | +3.3 V |
| Black | Ground |
| Purple | +5 V standby (on whenever plugged in) |
| Green | Power on: connect to ground to switch the supply on |
| Grey | Power good signal |
| Blue | −12 V |

## Network cable (Ethernet, T568B)

Pins 1 to 8, left to right, looking at the gold contacts with the clip underneath: white-orange, orange, white-green, blue, white-blue, green, white-brown, brown. T568A swaps the orange and green pairs. Old telephone wiring uses red and green for the line.

## Thermostat wires (24 V AC)

| Letter | Usual colour | Does |
|---|---|---|
| R (Rh, Rc) | Red | 24 V AC from the furnace transformer |
| C | Blue or black | Common: the other side of the 24 V (on some heat pumps blue is B instead) |
| W | White | Heat |
| Y | Yellow | Cooling (the compressor) |
| G | Green | Fan |
| O/B | Orange or dark blue | Heat pump reversing valve |

## Speakers and audio

- Speaker wire: the striped, ribbed or copper-coloured conductor is usually +. To check, touch a 1.5 V cell across the speaker: the cone moves out when + is on +.
- 3.5 mm audio plug: tip left, ring right, sleeve ground. Four-part phone plugs add a microphone: most since about 2012 are tip left, ring right, ring ground, sleeve microphone; older Nokia, Sony Ericsson and some Chinese phones swap the last two.
